faq.a: Selahattin is associated with the Arabic form صَلَاحُ الدِّين, whose core sense is selahattin; righteousness of the faith (turkish form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Selahattin?
faq.a: Selahattin is associated with Arabic. Selahattin is the Turkish form of Arabic صَلَاحُ الدِّين (Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn), meaning 'righteousness of the faith'. It was borne by Saladin.
Yes — the underlying form صَلَاحُ الدِّين is Arabic.
Selahattin can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Selahattin should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn is a compound of Arabic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Selahattin mean in Urdu?

faq.q: What does Selahattin mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Selahattin is rendered صلاح‌الدین and carries the sense صلاح‌الدین، صلاح دین.
A romanized syllable approximation is se-la-hat-tin. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Selahattin, selahattin. Script forms are صلاح الدين, صلاح الدین, صلاح‌الدین, صَلَاحُ الدِّين, सलाहुद्दीन.
